takeaway: IMN has tropical wave OT#45 crossing this afternoon–evening with ITCZ interaction and thunderstorms near the Nicoya Peninsula tonight along the Pacific coast, while Nicoya heat climbs near 37°C. No tropical cyclone near Costa Rica; EPAC development stays well offshore southwest of Mexico or farther west. Midweek ensemble means now lean more toward Pacific SW moisture flow and flanking lows than yesterday’s lighter easterlies — still a watch, not a locked temporales.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sat–Mon)
periods.pattern: Today: IMN Pacífico Norte — partly cloudy with gulf-area rain possible on the regional table; general commentary flags OT#45 + ITCZ, afternoon storms near the Nicoya Peninsula, and overnight rains along the Pacific coast. Heat: Nicoya max ~37.1°C. Sun–Mon: shower/storm chances continue as wave/ITCZ influence lingers. GFS 06Z and ECMWF 00Z 24-h maps keep Nicoya mostly light (~0.05–0.5 in / 24 h) through Sun morning; GEFS mean into Mon morning similar (~0.1–0.4 in). Papagayo lighter (NHC).
periods.implications: Mornings remain the better outdoor window; plan around this afternoon–evening convective window, especially near Nicoya. Heat is a real limiter.
periods.confidence: High for OT#45 timing and no nearby TC (IMN + NHC). Moderate on exact Nosara storm timing/amounts (IMN wetter language vs light–moderate model maps).

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Tue–Fri)
periods.pattern: Ensemble means (GEFS 06Z, EPS 00Z, AIFS-ENS 00Z) around Tue–Thu show flanking Caribbean/EPAC lows and increasing W–SW 850 hPa flow over Nicoya rather than yesterday’s light easterlies — more supportive of Pacific-side moisture, but 24-h Nicoya totals in means stay mostly light–moderate with heavier cores often offshore. Deterministic GFS 06Z is wetter/more aggressive locally (weak L near CR by ~Thu) and should not dominate. Not locked as a multi-day temporal.
periods.implications: Keep late-day plans flexible midweek; treat any wetter stretch as possible afternoon cells plus SW moisture, not a guaranteed temporales.
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued shower chances and a moister Pacific-side flow signal midweek; low–moderate for sustained temporales or a closed Central American gyre.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: IMN sub-seasonal (21 Sep–18 Oct) still keeps Pacífico Norte below normal (weekly Pac Norte roughly 5–90 mm) with stronger-than-usual trades limiting Pacific-side rain. CPC GTH (valid 23 Sep–6 Oct, text updated 15 Sep) favors below-average Caribbean rainfall weeks 2–3; EPAC genesis risk is coastal Mexico / open EPAC, not CR. Single GFS frames can still show a wetter day later — treat as scenario only.
periods.implications: No official signal for a prolonged flood-season spike on the Nicoya Pacific side; short heavy cells remain possible.
periods.confidence: Moderate for below-normal / no major local TC theme; low for day-by-day rain.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Roughly mid–late next week (~Tue–Thu 22–24 Sep) if flanking lows and sustained Pacific SW low-level flow persist
gyreWatch.supporting: GEFS mean 06Z f120 (~Thu 24) shows a ~1005 hPa L south of CR/Panama with W–SW 850 flow over Nicoya; EPS mean 00Z f120 shows a broader ~1001 hPa L over southern Mexico/northern CA with SW flow over CR; AIFS-ENS 00Z f120 also has W–SW Pacific-side flow; GFS deterministic 06Z f120 places a weak L near CR with onshore SW flow. Short-term IMN OT#45/ITCZ language supports a wetter weekend start.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Short-range GFS/ECMWF/GEFS precip maps keep Nicoya mostly light–moderate; AIFS-ENS f120 still has a western-Caribbean high rather than a closed gyre centered on CR; NHC has no disturbance near Costa Rica; IMN sub-seasonal still favors Pacific rainfall deficit. Ensemble means only — no member-count probabilities. One dramatic GFS frame does not establish a gyre.

whatChanged: OT#45 is now today’s IMN regional story (yesterday’s weekly text still framed it as Sunday — treat the daily regional as authoritative). Heat ticks up (Nicoya ~37°C). Papagayo has eased vs yesterday’s fresher E flow. Biggest model shift: midweek ensemble means (GEFS/EPS/AIFS-ENS) now show more Pacific SW moisture / flanking lows around ~Thu 24 than Friday’s light-easterly means — gyre watch rises from quiet watch-only to elevated watch, still not established.
practical: Best apparent outdoor windows: mornings Sat–Mon before convective peaks; today afternoon–evening is the period to plan around if OT#45 verifies near Nicoya. Worth planning around: heat (IMN Nicoya max ~37.1°C), possible storms today into tonight, and lighter Papagayo N–NW ~10 kt with seas ~3–5 ft today becoming light/variable Sunday (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113).
